name: Chase unpaid invoices
summary: Chases unpaid invoices: reads what is overdue in Xero, drafts each reminder at the right step of the ladder in the business's mailbox, and queues the send for approval. Crons read and draft; a person approves every send.

covered_by.aging-review: refresh and summary (overdue list read from Xero, weekday digest drafted)
covered_by.payment-receive: refresh (an invoice that leaves the open list is closed)
covered_by.phone-call: summary (invoices past the last reminder are flagged for a call)
covered_by.collections-or-write-off: approval (a person decides; nothing is written off automatically)
covered_by.reconcile-record: not covered (manual reconciliation is its own workflow, see gaps)
covered_by.invoice-issue: not covered (raising invoices is the invoicing workflow)

crons.name: refresh
crons.summary: Read the authorised invoices from Xero, record what is overdue, and close any invoice that has been paid or voided.

crons.name: draft
crons.summary: Draft the reminder for each invoice past a ladder step and queue its send for approval. (21:30 UTC is 7:30 or 8:30 am in eastern Australia.)

crons.name: summary
crons.summary: On weekdays, draft one overdue digest to the owner. It is a draft, never sent by the cron.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: reads from Xero, an Outlook draft in the business mailbox (including the owner's digest), and nothing else. Sending the reminder and noting it on the invoice in Xero are live operations and wait for a person.

xero.covers: authorised invoices, client contact and email, invoice PDF, invoice history note after a reminder is sent

microsoft-365.covers: reminder drafts and the owner digest in Outlook, the send of an approved reminder

gaps: Ignition: not in the kit, so direct debit is not read. Ignition's own failed-payment list is the place to look until it is mapped.
CRM: not a kit platform, so the CRM is not read or written by this workflow.

Telegram and OpenClaw (owners' own alerts and morning reports): the kit's Telegram sendMessage is a live send and no alert is wired. The digest draft replaces the morning report until that is decided.
Reply detection: the crons do not read the mailbox for replies or disputes. Until that is built, a person adds the client's Xero ContactID to pause_contacts when a reply needs handling.

Approval time check: an approved reminder is sent as drafted. The approval does not re-check Xero, so an invoice paid after the draft but before approval can still be chased. The approver checks Xero first (the approval text says so).
Xero's own invoice reminders: if they are switched on for the same invoices, the client gets two chasers. Check and switch off one before go live.
Phone chasing, payment plans, disputes and write-offs stay with a person. The workflow only lists who is past the last reminder.
Reconciliation is manual and is not integrated with Xero here, so it is not covered.

Both adapters are docs-only until a Xero demo company and a Microsoft 365 developer tenant prove them. The platform evidence file (all-payment-chasing-platforms.json) was not present, so platform support was taken from the kit's ops.json and the vendor specs only.
